chapter: Oakland and the Bay Area scene
title: Barbary Coast colored spots and local union restrictions
summary: Only two Black venues in San Francisco, and how Local 6 kept white proprietors from hiring Black musicians.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Matt Wilkerson, he run what they call a cavalry over there, trying to think, Bancroft, that was the name of it. And that was the only two colored spots they had around here in San Francisco. And all the rest of them were white places. And during that time, why local Sikhs were so strong, they said all the territory belongs to them and it was frightening the proprietors from hiring colored musicians. So that's the only two places you had to work. Whereas I said I used to go in and out waiting for my discharge. I was around here about a month before I got discharged. So by going there, sitting up there playing for the tips, he offered me a job. So when I got discharged, I went to Los Angeles, come back up here and work a while.
Can you remember when Sid LaFrawley was up here too? You said you first played with him down the road. In Los Angeles. No, not Sid in Los Angeles.
It was here then. That's what I mean.
Yeah, on the Barbara Coast, yeah, San Francisco.
Well, you maybe played with him down there too.
No, I can't recall him being down in Los Angeles.
He came right here then, you think?
Oh, another thing we didn't cover was the Tennessee 10, if Mr. Wright can help you out a little bit. Yes, he can because he can call Slow Kid's name and I can't call it.
